memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac, and he himself carried the fire and the knife. As the two of them went on together, Isaac spoke up and said to his father Abraham, "Father?" "Yes, my son?" Abraham replied. - Gen 22:6-7a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A quiet, tender, and deeply significant detail: "Abraham... placed [the wood] on his son Isaac." Isaac carried the wood for his own sacrifice up the mountain. Father and son walked on together, one bearing the wood, the other the fire and the knife. And then the child's trusting voice: "Father?"

The tenderness here is almost unbearable. "As the two of them went on together" - that phrase, repeated in this chapter, captures the closeness of a father and his beloved son walking toward the hardest moment imaginable. And Isaac's simple "Father?" reveals a child's complete trust, unaware of what lay ahead.

But there is something here that points far beyond Abraham and Isaac. Many years later, another Son would climb another hill outside Jerusalem, carrying the wood of His own sacrifice - the cross - upon His shoulders. "Carrying his own cross, he went out to the place of the Skull" (John 19:17). Isaac carrying the wood up Moriah is a shadow of Jesus carrying His cross to Calvary.

Scripture is quietly weaving a pattern that will only become fully clear in Christ. The beloved son, the wood laid upon him, the mountain of sacrifice - all of it whispers of the greater Son who would truly be offered. As you picture Isaac climbing that hill, let it move your heart toward Jesus, who carried His cross for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How does Isaac carrying the wood point you toward Jesus carrying His cross?
- Have you paused to consider the cost of the sacrifice made for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, as Isaac carried the wood up the mountain, You carried Your cross to Calvary for me. Thank You for the sacrifice You made. Move my heart to worship as I consider what my salvation cost.
Amen.
